NetPerturb Report

Perturbation scores across targets and cell types

Published

September 25, 2026

1 Overview

This report summarizes 1045 perturbation scores from perbscore_all_targets.txt, covering 55 target(s) across 19 cell type(s), scored under 1 binding mode(s) (antagonist).

The gene regulatory networks these scores were computed from were inferred with GENIE3 (--network: genie3). Every score below is relative to that network type, so scores from a run using a different inference method are not directly comparable.

Every requested target gene passed QC checking.

3 Perturbation score distribution

All 749 log10 scores from every target and cell type pooled into one distribution. Pooled scores are typically bimodal: a low mode of near-zero values from genes the network barely leans on, and a high mode carrying the signal. Only the high mode is kept, cut at the 0.75 quantile (red line, -8.283). That retains 188 score(s) and drops 561 below the cut; a further 296 non-positive score(s) cannot be logged and are not shown either.

The left panel is every score, so the cut can be checked against where the two modes actually separate — move it with --score_quantile if the red line does not fall in the valley between them. The right panel is what the heatmap below works with, on its own axis.

The green dashed line in both panels is the Top 2.5% threshold (-7.659), the 19 strongest score(s) in the run. Those are the scores the heatmap asterisks mark.

4 Perturbation score heatmap

Scores are log10-transformed and cut as above, so the colour scale spans the high mode only. Tiles below the cut, and those whose score is non-positive, are shown as missing (gray). An asterisk marks a score in the Top 2.5% of every score in the run — 19 tile(s), at or above -7.659 on the log10 scale.

5 Knockout networks

Each knockout and the genes it moved. scTenifoldKnk zeroes the target’s outgoing edges, realigns the knocked-out network against the wild-type one, and scores every gene on how far it travelled between the two; the genes drawn here are the ones clearing FDR < 0.05. Use the menu to switch between the 0 target and cell type combinations.

The knocked-out gene sits at the centre and the genes it moved sit around it. A combined target such as A;B is a single joint knockout, with both genes’ edges zeroed together, so all of its genes sit at the centre, each linked to every gene the knockout moved. A node’s size follows its log2FC, scaled within the combination on display, so sizes rank genes against each other rather than across cell types. The ring is capped at the 25 strongest genes per combination; the table in the next section is not capped. Hover any node for its exact values.

log2FC here is the log2 ratio of a gene’s squared alignment distance to the mean squared distance of its run, so it says how far a gene moved and not which way it went. It carries no direction, which is why no edge on this figure has a sign to read off: every gene shown simply moved further than its run’s average.

scTenifoldKnk was not run for this session, so there is no knockout network to draw. Pass --sctknk to generate one.

6 Knockout differentially-regulated genes

Every gene clearing FDR < 0.05, across all cell type and target combinations and with no cap on how many are listed per combination. distance is how far the gene moved between the wild-type and knocked-out networks; log2FC is that distance squared over the run’s mean, logged; p.value tests it against the chi-square null and p.adj is the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within the run.

p.value is a direct function of log2FC, so the two rank genes identically and the FDR cut above is the same thing as a log2FC threshold. The knocked-out genes themselves are left out: they always move furthest by construction, so their rows say nothing about the knockout’s effect.

Currently 0 gene(s) clear FDR < 0.05, across 0 target(s) and 0 cell type(s).

scTenifoldKnk was not run for this session, so no differentially-regulated gene table is shown. Pass --sctknk to generate one.

7 Knockout gene set enrichment

What the knockout moved, read as processes rather than genes. Every gene is ranked by log2FC – the log2 of its squared manifold-alignment distance over the run’s mean squared distance, so the ranking is the one scTenifoldKnk’s own paper feeds to GSEA, centred on the average gene rather than on zero – and each gene set is scored on how concentrated it is at either end of that ranking. Use the menu to switch between the 0 target and cell type combinations.

NES is the enrichment score normalised for set size, and it is signed here. Read the sign carefully: the ranking is by how far a gene moved, not by which way it moved, so a positive NES says a set is crowded into the genes the knockout disturbed most, and a negative one says the set sat still while the rest of the network moved. Neither is up- or down-regulation – there is no direction of expression anywhere in the scTenifoldKnk output to recover.

Each dot is one gene set: position on the x-axis is its NES, size is how many genes of it sit in the leading edge, and colour is -log(p.adj + 1), running blue at the weak end of the cut through to red at the significant end. That statistic is close to linear near p.adj of 0, so it separates the marginal sets from the rest and treats everything below about 0.01 as equally significant; the exact p.adj of every set is a column of the table. Sets are drawn only if they clear FDR < 0.25, the 20 strongest per combination by absolute NES. Hover any dot for its exact values; the table below carries all of them, uncapped.

One thing to keep in mind reading any of it: the genes ranked here are the ones each knockout network was built on – every gene detected in more than 5% of the cell type’s cells, plus the targets – not the whole transcriptome. Enrichment is relative to that universe, so a pathway carried by rarely detected genes cannot show up here.

No gene set file was supplied, so no enrichment was run. Pass --gsea_gmt with a GMT for this run’s species alongside --sctknk.

Every gene set clearing FDR < 0.25, uncapped – the figure above shows only the strongest 20 of each combination. leading_edge_n is how many of the set’s genes sit in the leading edge, the stretch of the ranking that carries the set’s score, and it is what the figure sizes each dot by. The leading edge’s gene names are not repeated here; they are in sctknk/gsea_all_targets.txt alongside ES and the unadjusted pval. Set names longer than 50 characters are shown cut, with the whole name on hover – the column filter still searches the part that is not shown.

No gene set file was supplied, so no enrichment was run and there is no table to show. Pass --gsea_gmt alongside --sctknk.

8 Cell identity overview

The identities scored above, as they sit in the embedding. This is the cell set after downsampling, so the group sizes are the ones the networks were actually inferred from rather than those of the full object.

8.1 Cells per identity

Cells and genes each identity’s network was built from. 29,752 cells were used in total, across 19 identities (--n_cells 2000 per identity, --min_cells 500; genes: every rank-score network (GENIE3, scRank, hdWGCNA) is offered the same 3,372 of the object’s 27,899 genes (gene4use: --n_hvg 1000 variable genes plus the species’ transcription factors, drug targets and the requested targets), and each identity keeps those with counts in its own cells, 2,270–2,757 genes per network). In the cells panel the grey bar behind each is the identity’s size in the input object; an identity dropped for --min_cells has only that bar, in orange. In the genes panel the pale green part is gene4use genes with zero counts in that identity, which can have no edges in its network: hdWGCNA pads them with zeros, and GENIE3 and scRank have nothing to fit them on. 2 identities were dropped for having fewer than --min_cells cells after downsampling, and no network was built from them.

8.2 Target expression per identity

Mean expression of each target gene in each identity, over the cells retained after downsampling – the cells its network was built from. A combined target (A;B) is shown as its single genes, each on its own. Expression is log-normalised (counts per 10,000, then log1p), and the number under each value is the percentage of the identity’s cells with at least one count of the gene. A target that is barely expressed in an identity has little for that identity’s network to connect it to, which is worth keeping in mind when reading its scores above.

9.1 Running time per step

Every task of the run bar the report, from Nextflow’s execution trace. A step that fans out – one task per cell type, or per cell type and target – is averaged over its tasks; the time is each task’s own run time (realtime), not counting time spent queued. Summed over every task that is 22h 38m of compute, against 3m 21s of wall-clock time.
